about.title: Yorba Linda Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Yorba Linda is a city of about 67,973 people in Orange County, and much of its workforce spends the day in motion — landscapers, delivery drivers, home-service technicians, and contractors moving between job sites along Yorba Linda Boulevard, Imperial Highway, Bastanchury Road, and La Palma Avenue. When a shift ends with an injury, the path forward is often less clear than people expect. Workers' compensation in California generally covers medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault, and it is usually your only claim against your employer. But if someone outside your company caused the harm — a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a faulty tool, or another driver — a separate injury claim may exist alongside comp. In 2025, Yorba Linda recorded 91 injury collisions with 116 people hurt, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when many people are still on the clock. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Yorba Linda Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We look beyond workers' comp
items.desc: Comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver — can support a separate claim. The attorney you are connected with can evaluate both tracks.

items.title: Deadlines are handled early
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a two-year deadline. Getting connected quickly helps keep those windows open.

items.title: No cost to you, and no retaliation tolerated
items.desc: Our connection service is free, and network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. If an employer pushes back after you report an injury, that retaliation is illegal and can be addressed.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Imperial Highway while making a work delivery. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical treatment and part of your lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. Separately, the other driver is a third party, so you may also have an injury claim against them with a two-year deadline. An attorney can coordinate the two so they do not work against each other.

items.question: How soon do I have to tell my employer I was hurt?
items.answer: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days. Reporting sooner is better, and putting it in writing creates a clear record. Your employer cannot legally punish you for filing a claim.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle injury matters on contingency, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
